column1: # DERIVED from label-eval-open-images-mapping.tsv (sha256 606b35bc…) for docs/models.md §3.13: the
# 23 candidate labels of inference-service.md §39.7 (L5: §39.3's 29 without the six proxies) keep
# their rows byte for byte; every other label is `none` here, so `select` takes images for the 23
# alone and `evaluate` scores the 23 alone. ⚠ A row below that is `none` is NOT a judgement that
# the label has no class: see the committed mapping for that. This file only narrows the run.
# mapped onto Open Images V7's image-level classes, for scripts/inference/label-eval.py
# (`select`, and `evaluate --truth open-images`). Every candidate label has exactly one row.
# ⚠⚠ THIS FILE IS A SET OF JUDGEMENTS AND WANTS A HUMAN REVIEW. docs/models.md §3.12.3 lists the
# Open Images verifies a class on SOME images only: present, absent, or not looked at.
#   An image is POSITIVE for a label when any of its positive classes is verified present.
#   It is NEGATIVE when none is, and any of its negative classes is verified absent.
#   Otherwise the label was not verified on that image, and the image is in no figure of the label.
# ⚠ A negative class is one whose absence means the label's absence: `Animal` for `animals`,
# never `Dog`. Where the two columns differ, that is why.
# kind: one-to-one | one-to-many (by the number of positive classes) | thin | none.
#   ⚠ `thin`: there are classes, and fewer than 20 verified positives or 20 verified negatives in
#   a half of the corpus. Listed and counted, NOT scored. `none`: no class at all.
# fidelity: exact (the classes mean the label) | broader (they cover more than it) | narrower
#   (less) | proxy (they stand in for it; the note says how). Reported apart.
# pool: verified positives and negatives for the label among the 143 494 images of the Open
#   Images V7 validation and test sets whose Rotation is 0.0, which is what `select` chooses
#   from. `select` recomputes both columns and refuses this file when they disagree.
# Classes are named by display name (oidv7-class-descriptions.csv), `;`-separated.
# Columns: label<TAB>kind<TAB>fidelity<TAB>positive classes<TAB>negative classes<TAB>pool positives<TAB>pool negatives<TAB>note
